title: The Pokemon Game That Was Supposed to Delete Itself Is Back
summary: A video game that was designed to delete itself has come back to life, 20 years later. The game is PokePark: Fishing Rally, a mini-game for the Nintendo DS. It could only be downloaded at a pop-up Pokemon theme park in Nagoya, Japan, in the summer of 2005. The game was programmed to erase itself after 12 hours or once the handheld was reset. For years, fans wondered if it would ever be playable again. Now a collector named Daniel Quadri has what appears to be the only confirmed fully playable copy. Quadri said it felt surreal to switch on his DS, spend a quiet moment fishing, and feel the rush of reeling in a Gyarados. At the 2005 park, players could walk around the attraction, which was about the size of a Costco parking lot, and catch water-type Pokemon, a bit like an early version of Pokemon Go. Quadri sent his cartridge to the grading company PSA, and he has also said he would like to help preserve Fishing Rally by sharing the file with other DS systems.
why_it_matters: It shows that saving old games and sharing them can keep fun things from disappearing forever.
